media:group.media:title: Who Was Zheng He?
media:group.media:description:
Commanding a fleet of over 300 ships, it is surprising how little is known today about Chinese explorer Zheng He. Once a servant, Zheng rose to become an admiral and diplomat who played a key role in expanding China’s maritime and trade influence across the areas surrounding the Indian Ocean. Through seven major voyages in the early 15th century, Zheng solidified Chinese dominance in trade and exploration.
Discover more about the lives and journeys of some of history’s greatest explorers with our _PBS World Explorers_ collection: https://gopbslearningmedia.org/ZhengHe

media:group.media:description:

entry.title: Hamilton and Burr’s Common Ground: Land in Western New York

media:group.media:title: Hamilton and Burr’s Common Ground: Land in Western New York
media:group.media:description:
Despite their well-established political and personal rivalry, Alexander Hamilton and Aaron Burr had several things in common. They were heroes in the American Revolution who then became lawyers and public officials. The latter roles led to another commonality: They both purchased land after the war in Western New York. Their reasons for doing so differed, but they both related to restrictions on who could own land in the newly created state of New York. Compact History host Cory McCants explains.
Ideal for students grades 3-8, this video resource will encourage students to explore how similarities between people are not always enough to overcome differences and how new land ownership affected various people in Western New York in the aftermath of the Revolutionary War. Discover the Compact History: Liberty and Legacy collection on PBS LearningMedia to find support materials for this video: https://gopbslearningmedia.org/CommonGround
Looking for more original, entertaining, and engaging content from the local communities of Western New York and Southern Ontario? Explore: https://www.youtube.com/c/BuffaloTorontoPublicMedia

entry.title: Why Patagonia Needs Its Predators Back

media:group.media:title: Why Patagonia Needs Its Predators Back
media:group.media:description:
In Patagonia, native grasslands had been fenced off by farmers for a century. The land was planted with non-native grasses and populated with domestic sheep and other livestock. The fences kept native grazers, the guanaco, out of their ancient habitat. Native predators, the puma, preyed on penned-in livestock in the absence of the guanaco. Farmers then turned to hiring hunters to kill the pumas, which caused most of the pumas to abandon their longtime homes. To solve this ecological disaster, conservationists purchased several huge farms in this region. The experts then rehomed the livestock and removed the fences. Once guanacos were permitted to return to their original grazing areas in Patagonia, their natural predators — pumas — quickly came back as well. This resurgence of a balanced ecosystem is helping to heal the harmed native grassland biome.
Ideal for classroom learning for grades 6-12, these additional support materials on PBS LearningMedia will guide students to explore the interconnectedness of life with the land and encourage them to consider the negative impacts of historic uses of land and the positive impacts of applying modern understandings about keystone predators and their critical role in ecosystem resilience. https://gopbslearningmedia.org/PatagoniaPredators

media:group.media:title: All About Arbor Day
media:group.media:description:
While most holidays honor events in the past, Arbor Day is about looking to the future. All across the country, Americans plant trees to recognize the important role they play on Earth. Even though Arbor Day is celebrated on the last Friday of April, several states choose to observe it on different days to align with their local planting seasons. Celebratory activities on Arbor Day include tree planting events, workshops teaching people about local trees and how to care for them, and forest and park cleanups. Investigate how your local community honors the day, and help support the health of our planet!
Ideal for grades 3-5 classrooms, this video is part of a collection that supports lessons on the history of holidays and how they’re celebrated across the world. Explore the All About the Holidays Collection on PBS LearningMedia: https://gopbslearningmedia.org/ArborDay

entry.title: How Cultural Burning Can Mitigate the Wildfire Crisis

media:group.media:title: How Cultural Burning Can Mitigate the Wildfire Crisis
media:group.media:description:
As wildfires worsen across California, Indigenous stewards of the Yurok Tribe are reintroducing ancient cultural burning practices to restore fire resilience to forests. Fire is crucial for various healthy ecosystems — groups of living organisms in a specific area that interact with one another and their surroundings. Ecosystems that depend on fire actually need it to keep their balance and well-being. Discover the Yurok Tribe's Traditional Ecological Knowledge (TEK) to learn how ancient stewardship methods can be integrated into modern land management practices.
Ideal for grades 9-12, this video resource will engage students in communicating complex environmental ideas in creative, accessible ways — and to help them see the human stories behind climate solutions. Discover the _Dynamic Planet_ collection on PBS LearningMedia for support materials for this video. https://gopbslearningmedia.org/CulturalBurningWildfires

media:group.media:title: Happy 100th Birthday, Sir David Attenborough!
media:group.media:description: In honor of Sir David Attenborough's 100th birthday, we're celebrating the naturalist, storyteller, and beloved voice who revolutionized how the world sees nature—and exploring how you can bring that same sense of wonder into your classroom. From collecting fossils as a child to pioneering underwater photography, Attenborough's journey is one of curiosity, passion, and an unshakeable love for the natural world. He didn't just document nature. He helped define what a nature documentary could be.

media:group.media:description:

entry.title: How is Nature Flexing Its Resilience in Our Changing World?

media:group.media:title: How is Nature Flexing Its Resilience in Our Changing World?
media:group.media:description: Science teacher Susan Chyczewski shares why the Evolution Earth collection on PBS LearningMedia is a game-changer for science classrooms. From zebra finches passing extreme heat-tolerance genes to their babies, to anoles evolving in the aftermath of back-to-back hurricanes, this collection brings real phenomena into the classroom and answers the question students always ask: "Why do we need to learn this?" Explore positive, real-world case studies of ecosystem succession, surprising animal adaptations, and natural selection in action—all grounded in wonder and hope.

entry.title: Whose (Revolutionary Era) Line Is It Anyway? #4

media:group.media:title: Whose (Revolutionary Era) Line Is It Anyway? #4
media:group.media:description:
Use this fun video to test your students' knowledge of Revolutionary Era figures and their famous quotes!
Spoiler alert! Answer revealed below.
New York social studies teacher Mary Kate Lonergan provides the context students need to truly understand one of King George III's most revealing quotes, written in a private letter to his longtime friend and hand-selected Prime Minister, Lord North, on June 11, 1779 — just 10 days before Spain would declare war on Great Britain. From his childhood friendship with Lord North to his unwavering refusal to relinquish the 13 colonies, the video explores how King George III's fear of losing his empire kept a war burning for over eight years and what that stubbornness ultimately cost him. This short video is perfect for sparking discussion about the British perspective on the Revolution and why understanding the man on the other side of the fight is essential to knowing the full story.
Check out the classroom support materials here: https://bit.ly/KingGeorgeWhoseLine
Check out THE AMERICAN REVOLUTION Classroom Collection here: https://bit.ly/KGAmericanRevolutionCollection
